title: Does selenium increase excretion of mercury or arsenic?

grade.title: At least one good randomized trial, or consistent human evidence from more than one source
grade.outcome: Urinary excretion of mercury or arsenic
grade.basis: Two randomized trials, n=103 and n=405, on excretion surrogates.

answerHtml: A randomized trial in a mercury-mining area found higher urine mercury and lower oxidative markers with selenium-enriched yeast. A larger randomized trial in adults with chronic arsenic exposure found higher urine arsenic and dimethylarsinic acid with selenium-rich lentils, and lower asthma and allergy incidence. Both are excretion findings. They are not trials of removing metal already stored in organs.

sections.heading: Trials
sections.html:
• Li 2012: 53 versus 50 residents of a mercury-mining area, 3 months, selenium yeast versus non-selenium yeast. Higher urine mercury and lower MDA and 8-OHdG. PMID 23033886.
  • Smits 2019: double-blind, 405 adults with chronic arsenic exposure, 6 months, selenium-rich lentils versus placebo lentils. Higher urine arsenic (p=0.001) and DMA. Lower asthma and allergy incidence. PMID 31299617.
